cues: After the depression of the nineteen thirties and the war, Western states built welfare states, protecting citizens from unemployment, sickness and old age.
In nineteen forty four Franklin Roosevelt called for a second bill of rights: jobs, health, housing, education.
People remember freedom from want, the floor.
But Roosevelt's highest promise was to end special privilege for the few: a ceiling.
That pairing worked only inside rich nations.
When rights went global, the demand for equality at home was dropped.
Then from the nineteen seventies, starting in Britain and America, governments turned to market fundamentalism and cut welfare.
The floor went global; the ceiling vanished.
